explanation: No Mathlib declaration states this verbatim: the only occurrences of `Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n : ℤ => Ioo (n : α) (n + 1))` are this theorem and its proof. But it is the case a = 0 of the more general Mathlib lemma `Set.pairwise_disjoint_Ioo_add_intCast`, which states `Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n : ℤ => Ioo (a + n) (a + n + 1))` under the same hypotheses `[Ring α] [PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedRing α]`. Instantiating a := 0 and rewriting `zero_add` yields the statement, in one line. That general lemma is proved from `pairwise_disjoint_Ioo_add_zsmul` (to_additive image of `pairwise_disjoint_Ioo_mul_zpow`), so it is independent of the theorem being judged; the library's current proof already uses exactly this derivation. I also checked the Ioc/Ico variants and the zpow/zsmul and intCast/natCast families for other declarations.
